messages:
sara: quick sync - following the hot/cold prototype, i'm proposing we ship the single-queue priority-coalescer as the default experiment. want to call out the concrete dequeue fastpath semantics and telemetry we need.

sara: motivation: keep kvcache locality and avoid doubling memory, while still recovering interactive p50/p90 wins from prioritizing short requests.

rick: outline the fastpath? is this just "if len_hint <= H and dequeue_wait < W then pick" or something smarter?

sara: good shorthand. implementer sketch: at dequeue time evaluate: 1) length_hint (sanitized) 2) request_age (how long it's waited) 3) current_latency_budget (measured on the worker for route/model). If (len_hint <= H && age <= A && budget < B) -> fastpath. Else normal.

oliver: two clarifications: (a) budget should be token-based remaining SLA window, not absolute latency now, (b) we need an anti-starvation bump so old long requests eventually get served.

sara: agreed. plan: bump priority for any request with age > T to avoid starvation. T tuned in experiment.

maya: how do we handle streaming/generate requests that arrive with unknown final length? length_hint may be omitted.

sara: default to conservative: treat missing hint as long. but add a cheap "first-frame token-count" probe for streaming where first N tokens can classify as short/long quickly.

liz: telemetry we need: per-tenant enqueue_age distribution, fastpath_accept_rate, misclass_requeue_rate, kvcache_eviction_rate, tail_latency_by_priority_bucket. also thread-level tracing for requeues.

sara: exact. plus an experiment metric: delta_p99_per_tenant and kv_evictions_delta. ci-bot should record those on perf runs.

ci-bot: perf-runner scheduled: suite priority-coalescer-proto. please tag the run with branch=priority-coalescer/v1.

rick: rollout strategy? 1) unit tests & fuzz for length-hint sanitizer (maya) 2) infra telemetry (liz) 3) bench 24h on canary node pool 4) A/B on 10% traffic for 48h then 50/50 if stable.
sara: yep. add kill-switch env var to disable fastpath at runtime.

oliver: question: batching interaction - if fastpath pulls short jobs first, does it starve batch formation for long jobs (they want longer batches for cost)? we should model throughput cost.
sara: good point. solution: when fastpath dequeues, it creates a separate micro-coalesce window W_fast that is small (e.g., 2-5ms) so it still allows microbatches for short jobs. long-job coalesce windows remain larger. ensures long jobs can still gather into efficient batches.

dan: does micro-windowing cause worker hot loops or CPU overhead? earlier experiments showed lots of scheduling churn.
rick: we should cap wakeups and use timer coalescing. implement dequeuer backoff: incremental backoff if no fastpath candidates.

maya: on length-hint sanitizer: i'll implement heuristics: clamp hint to [1, max_seq], map suspiciously small hints vs historical avg for tenant and mark as untrusted. expose trust_score in headers for scheduler.
sara: love that. scheduler uses trust_score to decide whether to admit to fastpath or require probe.

liz: dashboard plan: create an "A/B priority-coalescer" dashboard with: per-tenant p50/p90/p99, token-efficiency (tokens-per-second), kv_eviction_rate, requeue_rate, microbatch_size_by_priority. add alert: if kv_evictions_delta > 15% or p99_delta > 3% for more than 10min -> rollback auto.

ci-bot: perf-runner update queued: priority-coalescer-proto (branch priority-coalescer/v1)

oliver: performance hypothesis: expect p50 -10% to -15% for interactive tenants, p90 -5% to -10%, and p99 ~0% change if kvcache locality preserved. if kvcache worsens we'll see p99 up.

sara: AB experiment details: - population: 10% traffic control vs 10% priority-coalescer - duration: 48h - metrics: per-tenant p50/p90/p99, kv_evictions, tokens-per-GPU-second - success criteria: median p50 improvement >=8% and no tenant experiences p99 regress >3% or kv_evictions increase >12%.

rick: code notes: make dequeue fastpath pluggable so we can iterate heuristics without restart. also add traces for "fastpath-decision" with fields: hint, age, budget, trust_score, result.

sara: ops note: add a temporary runbook for rapid rollback with memory/gpu pressure signals: scale-down, disable fastpath, flush caches.

dan: any thoughts about per-tenant opt-in for partitioned kvcache (the lane approach) for big customers? we should keep that feature but behind an enterprise flag.
sara: agree. keep lane partitioning gated and documentation: "high-memory isolated lane - reserved kvcache - requires committed capacity". sales can pitch it as SLA-backed option.

maya: i'll start sanitizer PR and unit tests. linking a small fuzz harness for lying clients.

liz: i'll mock up dashboards and alerts, and wire CI hooks for perf-runner results.

sara: i'll draft the experiment runbook and add to the RFC follow-up. branch by EOW, canary 24h, A/B next week.

ci-bot: perf-runner started: 2026-03-22T01:08Z, suite: priority-coalescer-proto

rick: thanks team. excited to see if we can get most wins without the memory tax. :rocket:
